description: The SCRIPT//GO runtime contract, language-neutral. It describes what the kits expose to resources today; docs/spec/runtime-idl.md explains the format, docs/spec/multi-language.md the semantics across languages. Typings are generated from this file (tools/gen-types.mjs -> packages/types).

lua.failure: A call that can fail answers nil (or false) followed by a reason string; misuse (wrong argument types, calls outside a thread) raises a Lua error.
lua.sandbox: string, table, math, utf8, os.time/clock/date/difftime, pcall, xpcall, error, assert, select, type, tostring, tonumber, pairs, ipairs, next, rawget/rawset/rawequal/rawlen, setmetatable (no __gc), getmetatable, unpack, collectgarbage("count"). No io, debug, package, load, loadstring, dofile, loadfile, coroutine.

js.failure: A call that can fail throws a ScriptGoError whose code is the reason; asynchronous calls return promises that reject with one. Misuse (wrong argument types) throws a TypeError.
js.sandbox: ECMAScript built-ins only. No eval, no new Function, no require, no process, no CLR access.
js.typescript: scriptgo pack and scriptgo verify compile each .ts entry with esbuild 0.25.12 into <entry>.js (one IIFE bundle per entry, ES2022), placed next to the .ts in the archive or in the copy verify runs; a host loads <entry>.js, or fails with typescript_not_compiled:<entry>.
typescriptPreamble: /** Native modules registered by the host integrator. Their generated declarations (ScriptGo.Host NativeModule.ToTypeScript) merge into this namespace. */
declare namespace ScriptGoNatives { const __modules: unique symbol; }

cs.note: Phase 3. No C# guest exists yet: no kit runs .cs scripts and manifests that list them are refused (unsupported_script). This IDL has no C# bindings.

lua-core.note: The pure-Lua portable host every Lua-only adapter embeds.

dotnet.note: The .NET host kit: Lua guests on KeraLua, JavaScript guests on Jint.

capabilities.events: Local events, network events between sides, lifecycle events.
capabilities.logging: ScriptGo.log and print routed to the host log.
capabilities.players: Player list, names, join and drop events.
capabilities.permissions: Host privileges for a player (operators, privs, ACE).
capabilities.commands: RegisterCommand from the console or chat.
capabilities.ui: ScriptGo.ui.notify: on-screen notifications or chat fallback.
capabilities.http: Outbound HTTP requests from the server side.
capabilities.licensing: License activation and verification against the SCRIPT//GO API.
capabilities.perks: Player perks: what the operator sold to a player from their own store, asked from the SCRIPT//GO API.

value.doc: Any value the codec copies: nil, boolean, integer, number (finite), string, or an acyclic table with string or integer keys (see codec).

any.doc: Anything, including values the codec refuses (only for calls that never copy, such as print).

nil.doc: No value: nil in Lua, undefined in JavaScript.

integer.doc: A 64-bit integer in Lua; a number with no fractional part (within +-2^53) in JavaScript.

string.doc: Bytes in Lua, UTF-16 text in JavaScript; copied as UTF-8.

table.doc: A Lua table; an array or a plain object in JavaScript.

PlayerId.doc: A player id, >= 1. 0 stands for the console (commands, permissions); -1 targets every player (TriggerClientEvent, ui.notify).

Language.doc: The guest language running the calling code.

Notification.doc: A UI notification. The host adds a resource field with the sender's name.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: Header names as the server sent them, sorted

Manifest.doc: The parsed manifest of the calling resource, with camelCase field names (docs/spec/manifest.md).

ThreadFn.doc: Lua: runs in a scheduler coroutine. JavaScript: may be async.

params.name: args
params.doc: The words after the command name (Lua: a table with n)

params.name: raw
params.doc: The whole line, without a leading slash

ExportFn.doc: Lua: returns its values. JavaScript: returns one value, ScriptGo.values(...) for several, or a promise (async exports only).

LuaPromise.doc: A Lua promise: p:await() -> values... or nil, reason (inside a thread); p:next(onResolved, onRejected); p:status(); p:isSettled(); p:resolve(...); p:reject(reason).

Values.doc: Several return values from a JavaScript export, built by ScriptGo.values(a, b, ...).

errors.capability_unavailable:<capability>@<env: The host does not provide that capability.
errors.language_unavailable:<language>@<environ: The host has no guest for a language the resource's scripts use (the resource does not start).
errors.typescript_not_compiled:<entry>: A .ts entry has no compiled <entry>.js next to it (run scriptgo pack or scriptgo verify).
errors.resource_preparing: An export was called from file scope while the calling resource is still loading.
errors.resource_stopped: The calling resource side was stopped.
errors.invalid_event_name: Event names are non-empty strings of at most 128 characters.
errors.invalid_target: A client target is a player id >= 1 or -1.
errors.client_only: Only the client side may call this.
errors.server_only: Only the server side may call this.
errors.network_unavailable: The host does not run the other side.
errors.event_queue_limit: The host's queue of events for the next tick is full.
errors.event_payload_not_serializable: An event argument was refused by the codec.
errors.invalid_export_name: Export names are non-empty strings of at most 64 characters.
errors.export_not_found: The target resource side has no export of that name.
errors.export_resource_unavailable: The target resource is not started, or has no such side.
errors.export_yielded: A synchronous export call reached code that waits (Wait, await).
errors.export_recursion_limit: Synchronous export calls nested deeper than the host allows.
errors.export_arguments_not_serializable: An export argument was refused by the codec.
errors.export_result_not_serializable: An export result was refused by the codec.
errors.export_failed: <message>: An asynchronous export raised or rejected.
errors.export_target_stopped: The target resource stopped before an asynchronous export finished.
errors.invalid_path: A resource path is not relative, uses .., a drive letter or a leading /.
errors.not_found: No such file in the resource.
errors.invalid_module_name: require: module names are dot-separated words, or @dependency[/a.b].
errors.module_load_failed: <message>: require: the module does not compile.
errors.dependency_not_declared:<resource>: require("@lib") names a resource the manifest does not depend on.
errors.invalid_request: http.request and licensing calls need an options table.
errors.invalid_url: http.request needs an absolute http or https URL.
errors.http_failed: <message>: The HTTP request failed or timed out (30 s).
errors.http is server-side only: ScriptGo.http.request called on the client side.
errors.licensing is server-side only: ScriptGo.licensing called on the client side.
errors.invalid_response (<status>): licensing: the API answered something that is not JSON.
errors.http_<status>: licensing: an HTTP error without an error code in the body.
errors.duplicate command '<name>': Another resource side already registered that command.
errors.promise_rejected: A promise was rejected without a reason string.
errors.promise_already_settled: Lua: resolve or reject on a settled promise.
errors.await_requires_scheduler_coroutine: Lua: await outside a thread on a pending promise.
errors.quota_exceeded:instructions: The resource side ran more instructions (Lua) or statements (JavaScript) than its budget for one host-level entry.
errors.quota_exceeded:memory: Lua: the state's heap went over its cap (the resource stops). JavaScript: the entry allocated more than its cap (the entry is abandoned).
errors.quota_exceeded:time: JavaScript: one entry ran longer than its wall-clock budget.
errors.quota_exceeded:threads: Too many live threads (Lua coroutines, pending JavaScript timers).
errors.quota_exceeded:handlers: Too many event handlers on one resource side.
errors.quota_exceeded:exports: Too many exports on one resource side.
errors.native_unavailable_on_side:<side>: The native function is declared for the other side.
errors.permission_denied:<permission>: The native needs a permission the manifest does not declare or the host does not grant.
errors.invalid_argument_count: A native received more arguments than it declares.
errors.invalid_argument:<name>: A native argument does not match its declared type.
errors.native_arguments_not_serializable: A native argument was refused by the codec.
errors.native_result_not_serializable: A native result was refused by the codec.
errors.native_failed: The native handler threw (the host log has the message).
errors.codec: <reason>: The codec refused a value: codec: cannot transfer a function, codec: cyclic table, codec: value nested deeper than 32, codec: value exceeds 1 MiB, codec: non-finite number, codec: table keys must be strings or integers, ...

globals.name: CreateThread
globals.doc: Starts fn in a scheduler thread. It inherits the caller's source.

lua.doc: Runs fn in a coroutine until its first yield.

js.doc: Calls fn now; an async fn continues after each await on later ticks. Errors and rejections are logged.

globals.name: Wait
globals.doc: Suspends the calling thread for ms milliseconds. Wait(0) resumes on the next host tick.

lua.doc: Yields. Raises when called outside a thread (file scope).

globals.name: SetTimeout
globals.doc: Runs fn once after ms milliseconds.

globals.name: ClearTimeout
globals.doc: Cancels a timer from SetTimeout (or setTimeout in JavaScript).

globals.name: AddEventHandler
globals.doc: Handles an event on this resource side. Handlers run in registration order, across the languages of one resource.

lua.doc: Each delivery runs the handler in a new thread.

js.doc: Each delivery calls the handler; source is valid until its first await.

globals.name: TriggerEvent
globals.doc: Server: the host-wide bus; queued to the next tick, delivered to every started resource in resource-name order, without source. Client: delivered now, inside this resource side only.

globals.name: RegisterNetEvent
globals.doc: Allows network events of that name to reach this resource side; with fn, also adds a handler (its id is returned).

globals.name: TriggerServerEvent
globals.doc: Client to server. Server handlers see the sending player in source.

globals.name: TriggerClientEvent
globals.doc: Server to one client, or every client with target -1.

globals.name: source
globals.doc: The player behind the code running now: the sender of a network event on the server, the player of playerJoining/playerDropped, the caller of a command. nil elsewhere.

lua.doc: Kept per thread: still valid after Wait in the same handler.

js.doc: Valid in the synchronous part of a handler or command only: read it before the first await.

globals.name: exports
globals.doc: exports(name, fn) publishes an export of this resource side. exports.<resource>.<name>(...) calls another resource's export synchronously, in any language: the export must finish without waiting. Values are copied through the codec.

lua.doc: Register: exports(name, fn) -> true or nil, reason. Call: exports.res:name(...) -> every value; a failure raises "export res:name <reason>".

js.doc: Register: exports(name, fn) -> true, throws ScriptGoError. Call: exports.res.name(...) -> the first value; a failure throws ScriptGoError(reason) with the message "export res:name <reason>". ScriptGo.exports.invoke returns every value.
declarations: * exports(name, fn) registers an export; exports.<resource>.<name>(...) calls one synchronously and
* returns its first value. Other resources' exports are typed any (so that noUncheckedIndexedAccess
* does not make every call optional): check what they return.

globals.name: GetInvokingResource
globals.doc: Inside an export: the name of the calling resource.

js.doc: Valid in the synchronous part of the export only.

globals.name: RegisterCommand
globals.doc: Registers a console or chat command. Names match ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$ and are case-insensitive; the handler runs on the next tick; restricted commands need the command.<name> privilege.

globals.name: GetConvar
globals.doc: A host configuration value, or the default.

globals.name: print
globals.doc: Logs at info level, arguments converted to text and joined with a tab.

globals.name: require
globals.doc: Loads a module of this resource (a.b -> a/b.lua, then a/b/init.lua) or of a declared dependency (@lib, @lib/a.b). TypeScript and JavaScript resources import modules at pack time instead (esbuild bundles each entry).

globals.name: Citizen
globals.doc: Citizen.CreateThread, Citizen.Wait, Citizen.SetTimeout and Citizen.Await(promise), for code written for FiveM-shaped runtimes.

globals.name: promise
globals.doc: promise.new() -> a LuaPromise.

globals.name: Open77
globals.doc: An alias of ScriptGo, so resources written for the open77 environment that use the portable subset run unchanged.

globals.name: ScriptGoError
globals.doc: The error every failing runtime call throws (or rejects with). code is the reason token.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: Extra data: the decoded body of a licensing error, or the detail of a refusal (a codec message, a native's 'expected string, got integer')

globals.name: console
globals.doc: console.log/info/debug/warn/error: arguments converted to text and joined with a space.

js.signature: declare const console: { log(...args: unknown[]): void; info(...args: unknown[]): void; debug(...args: unknown[]): void; warn(...args: unknown[]): void; error(...args: unknown[]): void };

globals.name: setTimeout
globals.doc: The web-style timer: calls fn(...args) once after ms milliseconds, on the host tick. Same timers as SetTimeout.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo
namespaces.doc: The SCRIPT//GO namespace. Lua also has it under the alias Open77.

members.name: values
members.doc: Wraps several return values for a JavaScript export: return ScriptGo.values(a, b).

members.name: ScriptGoError
members.doc: The ScriptGoError class.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.log
namespaces.doc: The host log, with the resource and side as origin. Always available.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.json
namespaces.doc: JSON with sorted object keys: the same value always encodes to the same text.

members.name: null
members.doc: JSON null. Lua: a sentinel (nil cannot be stored in a table). JavaScript: null.

members.name: object
members.doc: Marks a table to encode as an object even when it is empty or a sequence (Lua). JavaScript: returns its argument.

members.name: monotonic
members.doc: Seconds on the host's tick clock (float).

members.name: now
members.doc: Unix seconds; nil where the side has no wall clock (OPEN//77 client).

members.name: version
members.doc: The runtime API version, "0.1.0".

members.name: luaVersion
members.doc: The Lua dialect ("Lua 5.4", "LuaJIT" ...).

members.name: environment
members.doc: The environment slug (standalone, dotnet, love2d ...).

members.name: language
members.doc: The guest language of the calling code.

members.name: generation
members.doc: How many times a resource (default: this one) has started.

members.name: hasPermission
members.doc: Whether this resource's manifest declares the permission.

members.name: readFile
members.doc: A file of this resource, confined to its folder.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.net
namespaces.doc: Aliases of the network event globals.

members.name: call
members.doc: Calls an export asynchronously: the provider runs it in its own thread, so it may wait. Values are copied through the codec. The provider does not inherit the caller's source.

lua.doc: Returns a promise, or nil, reason; p:await() in a thread gives the values or nil, reason. From file scope: nil, "resource_preparing".

js.doc: Returns a promise of every value; it rejects with a ScriptGoError. Unlike Lua, it is not refused at file scope (no resource_preparing).

members.name: invoke
members.doc: Calls an export synchronously, like exports.res.name(...), and returns every value.

members.name: require
members.doc: Fails unless the host provides the capability.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.storage
namespaces.doc: Per-resource key/value storage with JSON values, persisted by the host. The client side has its own store.

members.name: set
members.doc: Stores a value; nil deletes the key.

members.name: keys
members.doc: Keys in byte order, optionally with a prefix.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.players
namespaces.doc: Server side. Invalid ids answer nil or false.

members.name: has
members.doc: A host privilege of a player; player 0 (the console) has every privilege.

members.name: notify
members.doc: Server: notify(target, payload) with a player id or -1. Client: notify(payload) for the local player.

members.name: get
members.doc: A per-resource configuration value, or the default.

members.name: request
members.doc: An outbound HTTP request, only where the host allows it. Times out after 30 seconds.

lua.doc: Waits for the answer: call it from a thread.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.licensing
namespaces.doc: POST {scriptgo_api}/v1/licenses/activate|verify. Needs the http capability too.

lua.doc: Waits for the answer: result, or nil, code, body.

js.doc: Rejects with ScriptGoError(code) whose detail is the decoded body.

lua.doc: Waits for the answer: result, or nil, code, body.

js.doc: Rejects with ScriptGoError(code) whose detail is the decoded body.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.perks
namespaces.doc: Player perks (docs/spec/perks.md): what the server's operator sold to a player from their own store. One implementation, the portable core's module sdk/lua/scriptgo/perks.lua, which Lua guests run; JavaScript guests do not have it yet. Needs the http capability and the server linked to the operator's account (the host setting scriptgo_server_token). A player is a PlayerId, or the identifier string ScriptGo.players.identifier gives.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the player has the perk now. Asked from the API when the player is not known yet or the answer is old; otherwise answered from the cache, which never trusts a perk past its period end nor past the offline grace of the last answer.

lua.doc: Waits for the answer: call it from a thread. true, { expiresAt, status, source } or false, reason.

members.name: list
members.doc: Every perk of the operator the player has now: { key, expiresAt, status }, sorted by key.

lua.doc: Waits for the answer: call it from a thread.

members.name: refresh
members.doc: Asks the API again about one player, whatever is cached.

lua.doc: Waits for the answer: call it from a thread.

members.name: purchaseLink
members.doc: A signed, short-lived link to buy one perk for one player, tied to that player's identifier. Answers the URL and when it expires (Unix seconds).

lua.doc: Waits for the answer: call it from a thread. nil, code, message on a refusal.

members.name: catalog
members.doc: What the operator sells: { key, name, description, interval, price, purchasable } for each perk.

lua.doc: Waits for the answer: call it from a thread.

members.name: on
members.doc: Calls handler(player, key, info) when a perk is granted or removed: a purchase, a refund, a chargeback, the end of a period. kind is "granted" or "removed"; player is the connected player with that identifier, or nil; info is { identifier, perk, reason, expiresAt }. Answers a handler id.

members.name: off
members.doc: Removes a handler by its id.

members.name: status
members.doc: { linked, configured, cursor, lastPollAt, lastError } of the perks client.

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.notifications
namespaces.doc: OPEN//77-compatible names for ScriptGo.ui.notify (the ui capability applies).

namespaces.name: ScriptGo.natives
namespaces.doc: Native modules the host integrator registered (docs/spec/native-module.schema.json): ScriptGo.natives.<module>.<function>(...). A module declared with global: true is also a global of its name.

js.type: Omit<typeof ScriptGoNatives, "__modules"> & { invoke(moduleName: string, functionName: string, ...args: unknown[]): any[] }

lua.doc: Every value, true when the native returns none, or nil, reason, detail.

js.doc: The first value (undefined when none); throws ScriptGoError(reason) carrying the refusal's detail in detail.

members.name: invoke
members.doc: Calls <module>.<function> and answers every value it returns. A module cannot be named invoke.

js.doc: ScriptGo.natives.invoke(module, fn, ...args) answers every value; throws ScriptGoError(reason).

events.name: onResourceStart
events.doc: A resource started (each started resource receives it, the new one included).

rules: Every value that crosses a boundary (event, export call, native call, storage, host call) is copied; guests never share objects.
Numbers must be finite. Lua integers stay integers; a JavaScript number with no fractional part within +-2^53 becomes an integer, any other number a float.
Strings are bytes in Lua and text in JavaScript; they cross as UTF-8 (invalid UTF-8 reaches JavaScript as U+FFFD).

Table keys are strings or integers. A table whose keys are exactly 1..n reaches JavaScript as an array; an empty table as an empty array; any other table as a plain object, integer keys written as decimal strings, keys in order (integers ascending, then strings in byte order).

A JavaScript array becomes a sequence (index i -> key i+1; holes and undefined are nil). A plain object (object literal or Object.create(null)) becomes a table: own enumerable data properties only, undefined and null values dropped, keys that are canonical integers ("0", "17", "-3") become integer keys.

Refused, with the reason: functions, Lua threads and userdata, JavaScript symbols, bigints, class instances, Map, Date, Promise and proxies, accessor properties, non-finite numbers, keys other than strings and integers, cycles (codec: cyclic table), more than 32 levels of nested tables (codec: value nested deeper than 32), more than 1 MiB of encoded data (codec: value exceeds 1 MiB).

quotas.doc: Defaults of the dotnet kit (HostOptions.Quotas). Budgets are per host-level entry: a resource side gets a fresh budget the first time it runs after the host enters guest code from outside; nested calls in that entry, including calls from other resources, draw on the same budget.

items.name: lua.instructions
items.effect: The running Lua thread raises; pcall/xpcall cannot swallow it; the resource keeps running.

items.name: lua.memory
items.effect: Allocations past the cap fail inside the guest; the resource stops (state failed).

items.name: js.statements
items.effect: The entry is abandoned; try/catch and finally do not run; the resource keeps running.

items.name: js.allocation
items.effect: As js.statements. Measured as .NET allocations on the host thread during the entry, the host's own marshalling included.

items.name: eventQueue
items.effect: TriggerEvent and network events fail until the next tick.

items.name: syncExportDepth
items.effect: The nested synchronous export call fails.
